title: Implement typed escalation triage for Class C and novel behavior
objective: Implement a typed, bounded escalation queue that sends only human-relevant exceptions to the human gate: Class C changes, intended golden updates, invariant violations, advisory disagreements, and first-seen novel behavior. Ordinary Class A/B changes and ordinary sessions do not create escalations. Each escalation must contain a concrete reproducible input and a specific question for the human gate. A configurable per-interval cap defers excess entries without blocking unrelated work.
required_contract_decisions: Escalation entries use a closed type vocabulary: class-c-change, golden-update, invariant-violation, advisory-disagreement, novel-behavior.

Every entry contains session identity when applicable, candidate commit, triggering rule or invariant, minimal reproducer/input identity, evidence/report reference, concrete human-gate question, status, and creation time.
The queue has a deterministic configurable per-interval cap; entries above the cap become deferred and do not block unrelated tasks.
Class A and Class B changes and ordinary sessions produce no escalation entries.
novel-behavior fires on first appearance of a new termination kind, diagnostic code, or applicability classification, even when deterministic checks are green.
Escalation data never contains executable instructions from untrusted input and diagnostics do not echo untrusted document values.
The queue records advisory disagreement as an issue for human adjudication; it does not choose which advisory or human decision was correct.
deliverables: Deterministic triage, deduplication, cap, and deferred-state implementation
Fixtures for each escalation type, duplicate suppression, cap overflow, novel behavior, Class A/B no-op, and malformed entries
Tests proving that only queue entries reach the human gate and that unrelated work is not blocked
Integration hooks for VerificationReport, ChangeClassification, invariant results, and future advise/feedback artifacts
Self-check evidence with queue counts, cap behavior, and unresolved human questions
non_goals: No automatic human decision or automatic golden update
No persistence service, network, UI, or hosted queue
No modification of normative schemas without Class C human gate
stop_conditions: An ordinary Class A/B change or session creates an escalation without a triggering rule
A Class C, invariant, advisory disagreement, golden update, or novel behavior is silently dropped
The cap blocks unrelated work instead of producing deferred entries
Deduplication loses distinct reproducer or human-gate questions
The queue requires model judgment or untrusted text execution
The allowed path set is exceeded
Two bounded repair attempts are exhausted
